newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels index slips further on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Brussels index slips further on profit-taking.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended down on Wednesday with investors clearing their decks after the bourse's strong performance in recent weeks.
In midday trading the index outperformed European bourses where inflation worries are re-emerging, but in the afternoon the difference narrowed.
Dealers said the fall in the Bel-20 index was largely due to profit-taking adding that the index would regain strength after consolidation to push upwards in coming weeks.
"After some profit-taking I think we could see the index passing the 1,900 mark by the New Year," said a dealer.
The Bel-20 index ended 7.56 points down at 1,859.35.
Final volume was 2.605 billion francs worth of Belgian shares.

Dealers were satisfied with the performance of Belgian Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet Holding DEXI.BR, which made its debut today, closing at 2,800 francs, up from its list price of 2,675 francs.
Some 11 million shares or 30 percent of Credit Communal were put on sale on November 8 in one of Belgium's biggest initial public share offerings.
Another stock dealers were watching was cement maker CBR which has seen renewed interest by investors as its put warrant expires next month, with a strike price of 2,350 francs.
CBR which gained 40 francs or 1.52 percent to close at 2,665 francs was the most heavily traded stock in value terms.

Steel maker Cockerill Sambre gained 0.87 percent at 116 francs, which one dealer said was a technical blip. The share price started falling several weeks ago on expectations it would leave the Bel-20 by the end of the year.

Elsewhere among financials profit-taking continued, lead by Generale Bank which fell 2.36 percent, pharmaceuticals firm UCB shedding 1.49 percent, and Union Miniere losing 1.38 percent. Dealers expected the stocks to continue upwards once consolidation ended.

Traders said child sex scandal allegations against Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo, which he denies, has not had much affect on the bourse. Adding that investors believed the government was strong enough to handle such scandals.
